findings.passage: “I am proud to join today’s effort to defend the modest gains our federal government has made on gun safety,” Attorney General Rayfield said. “Community safety is one of my top priorities, and I will continue to do everything in my power as Attorney General to protect Oregonians from gun violence.”
findings.note: Quoted in a DOJ release announcing Oregon and 15 other states joining to defend a federal rule on machine-gun conversion devices (forced reset triggers) and a federal rule requiring gun sellers to run background checks.

findings.motion: Oregon joins multistate filings to defend federal forced-reset-trigger classification and the federal 'engaged in the business' gun-seller background check rule
findings.note: As Attorney General, announced Oregon's participation in two multistate court filings backing two federal gun rules.

findings.passage: “Oregonians voted for this, and it’s time we move ahead with common-sense safety measures,” Rayfield said. “Today’s decision is a big step forward for gun safety in Oregon. This measure gives us the tools to make sure gun buyers go through background checks and get proper permits, helping to keep firearms out of the wrong hands and making our communities safer.”
findings.note: Statement after the Oregon Court of Appeals reinstated Measure 114 (permit to buy, closing the three-day background-check default, limit of ten rounds on magazines).

findings.passage: “We know there will be a lot of conversation around this, but the bottom line is that we’re committed to protecting the rights of responsible gun owners while doing what we can to reduce gun violence,” said Attorney General Rayfield.
findings.note: Same Measure 114 statement; says the office is committed to protecting responsible gun owners and reducing gun violence.

findings.passage: “These devices turn regular guns into machine guns, and there’s a reason they’re illegal. They’re designed to unleash rapid, uncontrolled fire, and they’ve been linked to deadly school shootings across the country,” said Rayfield. “The idea that the federal government would hand thousands of these devices back out into our communities is a serious threat to public safety.”
findings.note: Quoted in a DOJ release on the multistate suit against ATF over a settlement to redistribute seized forced reset triggers.

findings.motion: Oregon and 15 other attorneys general sue ATF over settlement to redistribute seized forced reset triggers
findings.note: As Attorney General, filed a multistate lawsuit to stop ATF from returning forced reset triggers.
